cim: Zoo York: How One Phone Photo Became a One-Minute AI Monkey Movie
cim_eredeti: Zoo York: How One Phone Photo Became a One-Minute AI Monkey Movie
szoveg_eredeti:
One reference photo, five messages to Krea Agent, twelve matching stills, and twelve five-second clips cut into a 90s home-video short

Zoo York began with one photo: a monkey walking across a New York street with a laptop under its arm. It was a cheap phone snapshot of an ordinary block. That one frame set the look for the whole project. The monkey is small, the street is plain, and the camera is low quality on purpose.

A few plain-English messages to Krea Agent turned that photo into twelve matching scenes. Each scene became a five-second clip in Seedance 2.5, and the clips were cut into a one-minute short that looks like 90s home video. This guide shows the whole process, with every prompt, so you can copy it.

Pick one image that already has the feel you want. You don’t need a mood board. One strong reference keeps every later image consistent, because each request can point back to it with “similar to this vibe.”

The whole image set came from five short messages. None of them was a long, engineered prompt. They read like notes to a coworker:

The second message did the most work. The first batch didn’t match, so the fix was to name a different model and repeat the goal: different scenes, same vibe. When results drift, change one thing and say why.

The final set has twelve scenes: watermelon, horse, ducks, office, flying carpet, piano, rooftop pool, lowrider, unicycle, mattress, hammock, and balloons. All of them were made with GPT Image 2.5 at 16:9 and 2K.

They look like one series because every prompt ended with the same sentence:

Only the scene changes. The camera, the light, the colors, the framing, and the setting stay the same. Write the ending once and reuse it for every image.

Each image went into Seedance 2.5 as the start frame, at 1080p, 16:9, and five seconds. The video prompt is short and always has the same four parts:

Here is the prompt for the opening clip:

Left: the start frame. Right: a frame from the Seedance 2.5 clip.

Keep it to one gag per clip. Five seconds is enough for one clear action and a zoom. If you ask for more, the model usually drops part of it. The Seedance 2.5 prompt guide covers camera and audio lines in more depth.

The last step is the edit, and it’s quick:

Krea Agent ran the project. GPT Image 2.5 made the twelve stills at 16:9 and 2K, and Seedance 2.5 turned each still into a five-second clip at 1080p.

Start from one reference image and end every prompt with the same sentence that fixes the camera, the light, the colors, the framing, and the setting. Only the scene changes from prompt to prompt. If a batch still drifts, tell the agent what is wrong and try a different image model.

Zoo York used five seconds per clip, with one gag each. Seedance 2.5 can make clips from 4 to 30 seconds, but short single-action clips are easier to control and easier to cut together.
